clue.text: Can this chaff make one slimmer?

definitions.meaning: to chaff is to tease, and good-humoured teasing talk is chaff as a noun
a person who bants, following William Banting's nineteenth-century reducing diet

explanation.surface: A dieter wonders whether light-hearted teasing could help someone lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: To bant was to follow the Banting diet, named after William Banting, an early slimming regime; so one who bants is a slimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaff and this word both mean playful teasing talk; the second sense is an old word for a dieter on Banting's regime.

clue.text: Like Kipling's fastest traveller

parts.note: Kipling wrote that he travels the fastest who travels unaccompanied

explanation.surface: A literary question about the speediest wanderer in Kipling's verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The line is from Kipling's poem The Winners: 'He travels the fastest who travels alone'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's quickest traveller goes without companions, which is to say solo.

clue.text: Change rough pit work for vegetable production

parts.note: to change is to turn, as milk turns

indicators.note: rough here means roughed up, so the letters of pit are jumbled

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A miner suggests swapping heavy pit labour for growing greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rough' turns PIT into IPT, set between TURN and OP.
explanation.definitionFit: The leafy shoots a root crop produces are eaten as greens, so they are a vegetable's production.

clue.text: I go into play with strictness

indicators.note: into means the first piece is put inside the second

parts.note: R.U.R. is Karel Capek's play that gave us the word robot
taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor joins a production that is run with severe discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: R.U.R. (Rossum's Universal Robots) is a 1920 Czech play by Karel Capek, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigour is severity or exactness, a synonym of strictness.

clue.text: King, for one, is on board

definitions.text: King, for one, is on board

parts.words: King, for one, is on board
parts.note: reads like a monarch being a company director, but the king is a piece on a chessboard

explanation.surface: A monarch has been appointed to a company's board of directors.
explanation.definitionFit: The king is one of the pieces used in chess, played on a board.

clue.text: Masses of German loot — coins, possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters given could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Heaps of plunder from Germany, perhaps in the form of coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges all fifteen letters of GERMAN LOOT COINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A conglomeration is a mixed heap or cluster, so these are masses.

clue.text: Making it possible for beginner of 28 to catch fish

indicators.note: the beginner of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: 28 across is ERRATA
to catch is to nab
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Helping a novice angler land a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginner of' takes E, the first letter of the answer to 28 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Enabling something means allowing or permitting it to happen.

clue.text: Point to inferior track

parts.note: S, south, is a point of the compass
inferior means poor in quality

explanation.surface: Someone indicates a second-rate path.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoor is the trail of an animal, its track or scent.

clue.text: Irritated, one goes into a roll manoeuvre

definitions.text: Irritated, one goes into a roll manoeuvre

indicators.note: goes into means the first pieces are placed inside the jumbled letters
manoeuvre says the letters of a roll are moved about

parts.note: irritated means mad, angry
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: An annoyed creature curls itself up into a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvre' makes AROLL into AR...LLO; 'goes into' puts MAD and I between. The whole clue describes the animal, which rolls up when threatened.
explanation.definitionFit: The armoured mammal curls into a ball when alarmed, which the clue paints.

clue.text: Errors, in general, in bullfight

indicators.note: in says the short piece is placed inside the longer word

parts.note: a corrida is a Spanish bullfight

explanation.surface: Mistakes, broadly speaking, are made in the bullring.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is part of 'in general' in the surface; it is the second 'in' that places GEN inside CORRIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrigenda are things to be corrected, a list of mistakes in a printed work.

clue.text: Circle warship showing measure of resistance

parts.note: O is the shape of a circle
HMS, His or Her Majesty's Ship, prefixes British naval vessels

explanation.surface: A naval ship encircles another to show defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical resistance is measured in these units, named after Georg Ohm.

clue.text: Remaining back to praise one's Queen

indicators.note: back says the whole run of pieces is read in reverse

parts.note: to laud is to praise
one's is I'S, one is I plus is
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A courtier returns to singing the monarch's praises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses LAUD + IS + ER, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Residual describes what is left over, so it means remaining.

clue.text: … having banished us, perhaps, to Spanish city

indicators.note: perhaps says the remaining letters are rearranged into a new word

parts.note: the ellipsis carries over the answer of the previous clue, 11 across

explanation.surface: Having thrown us out, someone may be heading for a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis brings in 11 across, RESIDUAL; 'having banished' removes U and S from it, and 'perhaps' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Lerida (Lleida in Catalan) is a city in Catalonia, north-east Spain.

clue.text: Injection that could be fatal

parts.note: a jab with a needle is one sense; a firing of a gun, possibly lethal, is the other

explanation.surface: A doctor warns that a jab might kill.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hypodermic jab and the discharge of a gun, which can kill.

clue.text: So impetuous, unlikely to have cold feet?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a warm head at the top of the body, with cold feet as the idiom for losing nerve

explanation.surface: A rash person is hardly going to lose their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: Cold feet is the idiom for nerves before a commitment; someone warm at the other end is not prone to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rash, quick-tempered people are described this way; the jokey second reading sets a warm top against chilly toes.

clue.text: Pipe of various kinds

definitions.meaning: a branching pipe in an engine carrying exhaust or intake gases

explanation.surface: A tube available in many different types.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine's branching exhaust pipe has this name, and the adjective means many and varied.

clue.text: Outsider in race

parts.note: reads like an unfancied runner in a horse race, but means someone of another nation

explanation.surface: A long-shot horse is entered in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien from another country or people is an outsider in nationality.

clue.text: Confused excitement in the home turn

parts.note: a flat is a home
a spin is a turn

explanation.surface: Panic sets in as a runner rounds the final bend for home.
explanation.walkthrough: A flat spin is a dizzy state of agitation, from an aircraft's uncontrolled spin.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a dizzy panic is an idiom drawn from an aircraft's uncontrolled horizontal spiral.

clue.text: He spots Saracen's Head boozer

indicators.note: Head of a word means its first letter

parts.note: a tippler is a habitual drinker, a boozer

explanation.surface: A drinker is spotted at the Saracen's Head, a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Saracen's Head is a common English pub name, so 'boozer' (a British word for pub) seems to belong with it, but here it means a drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Stippling is painting or drawing in dots, so one who stipples puts spots down.

clue.text: Accommodation booked by' Virginia Woolf?

parts.note: not a hotel reservation but the space in the title of Woolf's essay A ... of One's Own

explanation.surface: A novelist has reserved a hotel stay.
explanation.walkthrough: Booked means put in a book: Woolf's 1929 essay is A Room of One's Own.
explanation.definitionFit: A space to stay in is accommodation, and it is the key word of Woolf's essay title.

clue.text: Resist Dominican attitude

parts.note: OP, Order of Preachers, is the Dominican order
an attitude is a pose or posture

explanation.surface: A friar's stance is one of defiance.
explanation.walkthrough: Dominican friars put O.P. (Ordo Praedicatorum) after their names.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose something is to resist or stand against it.

clue.text: Doctrinaire ill-humour about Chaucer perhaps

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking
Dan was an old title of respect, as in Spenser's Dan Chaucer

explanation.surface: A dogmatic scholar gets grumpy over Chaucer.
explanation.walkthrough: Dan, an old honorific like Master, is applied to Chaucer by Spenser.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrinaire person sticks rigidly to theory, much as a stickler for rules does.

clue.text: A major optical defect, mainly on one side

parts.note: in the Gospel, the beam in your own eye outweighs the mote in your brother's

explanation.surface: A serious eye problem affects mostly one side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' points to the main, the sea: a ship's term for abreast of the vessel. The beam in one's eye is from Matthew 7.
explanation.definitionFit: At sea, an object at right angles to a ship's keel lies on one side of it.

clue.text: Vessel returns with another star

indicators.note: returns says the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a pot is a vessel
another vessel, here an ocean liner

explanation.surface: A ship comes back with a second one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns POT round; 'another' means another vessel, a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A headline act, the performer at the top of the bill, is a star.

clue.text: German statesman backed some valiant rebels

indicators.note: backed says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A German politician supported a few brave insurgents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes TREBE from valianT REBEls; 'backed' turns it round. Friedrich Ebert was the first president of the Weimar Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Ebert led Germany as the Weimar Republic's first president.

clue.text: Excitable on this border

parts.note: on followed by the word means nervous, and the word alone means a border

explanation.surface: Nervy guards patrol a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is a margin or rim, and to be on it is to be nervous.

clue.text: Declared to be marked

explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is announced formally, and a noticeable accent is strong; the word covers both.

clue.text: Eccentrics take turn in street scraps

parts.note: odd men are eccentrics

indicators.note: turn says the abbreviation is flipped round

explanation.surface: Weirdos take a stroll down the road picking up rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses ST to TS after ODDMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddments are leftover bits and pieces, which are scraps.

clue.text: Perhaps 9 at rare assembly

indicators.note: assembly means the letters are put together in a new way

explanation.surface: A rare gathering of items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps 9' defines by example: errata are one kind of corrigenda (9 across). 'assembly' rearranges AT RARE.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed printing mistakes, a kind of corrigenda, the answer to 9 across.
